newsitem.title: MEXICO: 13 arrested in Mexico smear video scandal.
newsitem.headline: 13 arrested in Mexico smear video scandal.

text.p: Police arrested and later released 13 Mexicans on Thursday in a growing scandal over an underground video smearing leftist leader Cuauhtemoc Cardenas and his party in the campaign for major Mexico City elections.

The incident flared when police raided a clandestine video-printing shop overnight in Mexico City's bohemian Condesa neighbourhood, in which authorities said 30,000 of the videos were stored and ready to be distributed.

But the Attorney General's Office said late on Thursday it had found no evidence that Mexico's electoral law was broken in production of the video -- which casts Cardenas and his Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) as violent radicals.
It said employees of the video shop, which was also found to produce pornographic material, were set free and that the shop's owners could also make bail.
"Despite charges by the PRD that this breaks electoral law ... we have determined no electoral crime was committed..." a statement by the Attorney General's Office said.
The video, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, shows Cardenas, front-running candidate for the July 6 mayoral race, promising a peaceful campaign and rejecting violence.
It then cuts to images taken over the past few years of radicals burning busses, hurling molotov cocktails and stoning police, some waving banners of Cardenas's PRD.

PRD officicals accused the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) of organising the video to hurt Cardenas. The Mexico City race is the first of its kind this century and political analysts say victory could propel Cardenas to the national spotlight.

"We caught them red-handed," Jesus Ortega, secretary general of the Party of the Democratic Revolution, told Mexico City's Radio Red. "This is part of the smear campaign against our party and against Cuauhtemoc Cardenas in particular."
But Alfredo del Mazo, the PRI's candidate who is running a distant second in the Mexico City race, denied he knew anything about the tapes and called for an investigation.
"Anything that in any way leads to a dirty war is inconveniant," he said. "Nothing like this should happen."
Mexican elections have long been plagued by charges of dirty tricks, that the opposition charges has helped PRI rulers maintain their 68-year grip on power.
The government has pledged that the elections, which include a federal vote to renew the 500-seat Chamber of Deputies, will be the cleanest ever.
The video is signed by two unknown groups: "Business Action" and "National Council of Popular Organisations".
